_port_note: THE ONE INJECTION SITE WITH NO LATCH AT ALL, and worse than that: the builder wrote a CONSTANT id while MAX_SHEETS allows more than one live sheet. Two sheets warning on the same day produced ONE card, and the survivor named the wrong investor's deadline. The player was told a true fact about the wrong company. Fixed by construction: the scope slot binds the investor and the latch is entity-keyed, so each sheet gets its own card. The investor slot selects `expiring_sheet`, not the first investor by id. Without a selector the slot would bind whoever sorts first and the card would name the wrong deadline — which is exactly the constant-id bug this port exists to close, rebuilt in the new vocabulary.
speaker: char_mentor_frank

tr.title: VC_EV_OFFER_EXPIRING_TITLE
tr.body:
{investor} teklifi masada.

Frank: "Yatırımcılar bekletilmeyi sevmez. {seam:funding.sheet_days_left} gün içinde yanıt vermeliyiz."

en.title: VC_EV_OFFER_EXPIRING_TITLE
en.body:
{investor}'s offer is on the table.

Frank: "Investors don't like being kept waiting. We need to give them an answer inside {seam:funding.sheet_days_left} days."

_copy_fix: THE BODY MOVED OUT OF THE CSV AND THE PROSE DID NOT CHANGE. As the key VC_EV_OFFER_EXPIRING_BODY it carried {investor} and {days}: the first resolves from the bound scope slot, the second resolves from nothing at all, so the player was reading a literal "{days}" inside a Frank line. {seam:} cannot live in the CSV - loc_csv_integrity counts braces against [a-z_]+ tokens and rejects it - so the body is inline here in both locales, exactly as customer/request_complaint.json carries its per-sector line. Only the machine token moved. Audited across every card body in data/events/: this was the only unresolvable token in the content set, and the new smoke case card_body_tokens_resolve now fails the build if a second one appears.
